EXAMINED AND DELIBERATELY NOT REPORTED:
- `userEvent.keyboard` still delivers keys only to the target's own controllers on 1.0.0, so a window-level `GtkShortcutController` never fires. That is F111, already fixed on `bugfix/v1.0` (packages/testing/src/user-event/keyboard.ts now builds a full capture/target/bubble propagation chain). Same for F109 (fake timers), F110 (type/paste appending), F206, F207, F208 — all reproduce on 1.0.0 because the fixes are unreleased.
- A bare `GtkListView` of >=2000 rows in the harness window kills the vitest worker with `Gdk-CRITICAL ... Unable to create Cairo image surface` (the harness grows to the child's minimum height: 23000px at 1000 rows). Ruled out: the identical tree in a plain `gtkx build` + `node dist/bundle.js` app dies exactly the same way, so it is GTK refusing a 46000px surface for an unscrolled list, not the harness. Wrapping in `GtkScrolledWindow` keeps the window at 800x600 and virtualizes to 27 rows. Left at tests/r2-biglist, r2b-threshold, r2c-realistic.
- `accessibleLabel` is silently ineffective on a `GtkButton` that also has `label`. Ruled out against gtk-4.22.4 source: `gtk_button_set_label()` sets `GTK_ACCESSIBLE_RELATION_LABELLED_BY` to the internal label, and `gtk_at_context_get_text_accumulate()` step 2.B puts labelled-by ahead of step 2.C's LABEL property, so GTK itself reports the visible label. GTKX agrees with GTK. (tests/r3-accessible-label)
- `@gtkx/testing` computes an accessible name from content for every role, whereas GTK's `naming[]` table restricts step 2.F to roles carrying `NAME_FROM_CONTENT`. Consequence: an unlabelled `GtkEntry` is reachable as `getByRole(TEXT_BOX, { name: "hello" })` by the text typed into it, and `toHaveAccessibleName()` passes for it, although GTK exposes no name. Not reported: the same fallback is what makes the tutorial's own documented `findByRole(LIST_ITEM, { name: /Water the plants/ })` work (an `AdwActionRow` carries no author-set LABEL either), so it is an intentional divergence, not a defect. Evidence left at tests/r6-name-from-content.
- An `AdwExpanderRow` given `children` instead of its `rows` slot parents the nested row directly and emits `Gtk-CRITICAL: gtk_list_box_row_grab_focus: assertion 'box != NULL' failed` on focus. This is the already-rejected R206 class (generated props accept `children` for elements with no children slot), so not re-reported.
- `userEvent.paste(widget)` with an empty clipboard throws a raw `GLib.Error: Cannot read from empty clipboard.` out of `Gdk.Clipboard.readTextFinish` instead of a testing-library error. Too thin to report on its own.

Worked the `lifecycle` surface against @gtkx/*@1.0.0 from public npm, in /home/eugenio/gtkx-playground/lifecycle-r5 (a copy of bughunt-template with applicationId changed to com.gtkx.lifecycler5 and each probe given its own applicationId so runs never collided with other hunters). WHAT I EXERCISED, CLEAN (no defect found):
- Cancellation matrix (src/pa.tsx): a Gio.Cancellable cancelled before the call, during the call (Gio.Subprocess.waitAsync on `sleep 5`, cancelled at 300 ms, rejected at 302 ms), after completion, reused after reset(), and shared by two concurrent calls cancelled in the same tick. Every case rejects with domain 773 code 19 (Gio.IOErrorEnum.CANCELLED); nothing hangs, nothing resolves that should reject. Matches website/guide/async-operations.md.
- quit() while async work is in flight (src/pb.tsx, pb2.tsx): a pending Subprocess.waitAsync on `sleep 20` plus a pending loadContentsAsync; quit() exits the process in ~2 ms with code 0. quit() called three times in a row, and quit() called from inside a close-request handler: both clean (src/pj.tsx).

confirmed.surface: @gtkx/cli — the shipped ambient module declarations in node_modules/@gtkx/cli/env.d.ts (`declare module "*.png"`, `"*.data"`, `"*.gpa"`, and 20 more), published as API reference at website/reference/env/_.png/variables/path.md etc., against the `gtkx:resources` plugin that implements them (dist/vite-plugins/resources.js, `dataAssetSource`, which returns null for any specifier not starting with `#data/`)

confirmed.expected: `declare module "*.png"` matches every specifier ending in .png, so the shipped types state that any asset import — relative or `#data/` — carries a GResource `path`, and that any `*.data`/`*.gpa` import's default is a `resource://` URI "accepted anywhere GTK takes a URI". Only the `#data/` form is: every documented example (website/tutorial/preferences-and-theming.md, the 1.0 blog post's "Assets imported through `#data/*` are staged, compiled with glib-compile-resources, and registered at startup, so an import gives you a `resource://` URI") and every shipped sample (examples/gtk-demo/src/**, e.g. `import { path as logoResourcePath } from "#data/icons/org.gtk.Demo4.svg"`) uses it. A user who writes the relative import that every other bundler has trained them to write gets told by tsc that it is correct, sees it run under `gtkx dev` with the value silently `undefined`, and only learns otherwise from a `gtkx build` rollup error — or, for `.data`/`.gpa`, never learns at all, because that one builds and then hands GTK a path where a URI was promised. The declarations should be scoped to the specifiers the plugin actually rewrites, or the plugin should handle every specifier the declarations claim; and `gtkx dev` must not resolve to `undefined` what `gtkx build` rejects outright.

confirmed.reasoning: Confirmed, and it is GTKX's integration defect, not Vite's and not the machine's. Reproduced the whole mechanism with a bare Node script against the repo's own vite 8.2.1 (/tmp/vite-restart-probe, no GTK, no compositor): with `server: { middlewareMode: true }`, writing `.env` or `vite.config.mjs` makes Vite log "changed, restarting server..." and run `restartServer`, which creates a fresh server, `await server.close()`s the old one, then `Object.assign(server, newServer)`. Probe output: `server.watcher !== firstWatcher` is true afterwards, the `change` listener attached before the restart never fires again for later source saves, and `server.moduleGraph` is swapped too (`getModuleById(entry)` goes true -> false). Vite's own `handleHMRUpdate` gates this on `file === config.configFile || config.configFileDependencies.some(...) || (config.envDir !== false && getEnvFilesForMode(...).includes(file))`, and `restartServerWithUrls` restarts in middlewareMode explicitly, so this is documented, deliberate Vite behavior an embedder must either opt out of (`configFile: false` / `envDir: false`) or re-bind to. GTKX does neither: `createDevServerConfig` (packages/cli/src/dev/vite-dev-server.ts:30) sets neither option, and `watchProjectFiles` (packages/cli/src/dev/runner.ts:338) attaches `add`/`change`/`unlink` exactly once, from `createDevRunner.run` (:539), to the watcher of the server instance it created. After the restart every listener is on a closed watcher, so no further save reaches `applyChange`. Even the triggering change is swallowed: today the `.env` path does reach `applySave` -> `applyModuleChange`, where `session.server.moduleGraph.getModuleById(changedPath)` returns undefined and the function returns at the bare `if (!module) return;` guard (runner.ts:215-219) without logging anything, which is exactly the reported "gtkx dev said: 0 lines". None of the rule-outs apply: no GTK/GLib API is involved; the docs warn against neither file, `packages/cli/env.d.ts` ships `/// <reference types="vite/client" />` (so `import.meta.env` and `.env` are supported inputs) and `builder.ts` loads the user's vite config for `gtkx build` as well, so both files are supported project inputs; it is not machine-specific (reproduced with plain Node); and it is a broken documented behavior, not a missing feature, since website/guide/getting-started.md:61 promises "Leave it running while you work" and the loop dies permanently and silently. Not a duplicate of any pre-round-5 entry: F113 is rapid-save staleness and F209 is the `change`-only subscription (already fixed in-tree by `WATCH_EVENTS = ["add", "change", "unlink"]` at runner.ts:69); both concern the contents of the subscription, while here the entire watcher object plus the module graph are discarded.

Confirmed, and none of the rule-outs apply. Not a GTK/GLib behavior, not documented misuse, not a duplicate, not machine-specific, and not a missing feature: an ordinary `npm install` destroys an artifact GTKX itself installed, and the project stops typechecking.

Reproduced with no GTKX in the picture at /tmp/npmprune: a package.json with no dependencies, `node_modules/.store/gi/package.json` naming `@x/gi`, and `node_modules/@x/gi -> ../.store/gi`. `npm install --offline` prints "removed 1 package" and deletes the link; `.store/gi` is untouched. npm's reify prunes every extraneous node in `node_modules`, and a dot-directory is not a node while a scoped link with a package.json is. Reproduced end to end on a copy of the template at /tmp/tmplcheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0, then a bare offline `npm install` removes both links and tsc reports TS2307 for `@gtkx/gi/gtk` and `@gtkx/jsx/gtk` in every source file while `node_modules/.gtkx/{gi,jsx}` is intact. pnpm 11.20 keeps the link, so this is npm's reconciliation, and npm is the package manager the tutorial uses.

GTKX owns the choice that npm punishes. `storeOptions` (packages/codegen/src/store/resolve-store.ts:86) sets `linkDir: join(nodeModules, SCOPE, name)`, and `swapStore`/`symlinkRelative` (packages/codegen/src/store/store-fs.ts:118, 108) plant `node_modules/@gtkx/{gi,jsx}` as the store's only entry point. website/guide/configuration-and-codegen.md:41 states the design outright: the store links into `node_modules/@gtkx` "so imports resolve without either appearing in your `package.json`", which is exactly the property that makes npm classify it as extraneous. The scaffolded tsconfig (packages/create-gtkx/src/templates/tsconfig.json.ejs) has no `paths`, so tsc and the editor's TypeScript server depend on that link alone.

Nothing re-checks it during a session. `gtkx dev` verifies the link once, at startup, through prepareProject -> ensureGeneratedIn -> isCodegenStale -> isGiStoreStale/isReactStoreStale (packages/cli/src/codegen/freshness.ts:33 and :45 both `existsSync` the link dirs); afterwards `resolveConfigWatch` (packages/cli/src/codegen/run-codegen.ts:240) hands the supervisor `paths: [resolve(root, configFile)]`, so only gtkx.config.ts is watched. The tutorial meanwhile tells the reader to keep `npm run dev` running for its whole length (website/tutorial/index.md:87) and then to run `npm install @gtkx/components` (trash-and-toasts.md:32) and `npm install zustand` (the-task-store.md:24) mid-session, with no instruction anywhere to re-run codegen after an install.

The report's second complaint, the misleading "have not been generated" message, is already fixed at HEAD and should not be counted: `unresolvedModuleError` (packages/cli/src/vite-plugins/undeclared-library.ts:98) checks `hasNamespaceModule(options.storeDir, namespace)` and branches to `unreachableStoreError` (line 72), which names the link path; the jsx manifest exports keys are `./adw` etc., so that branch fires in this scenario. The playground template carries an Aug 11 build predating it. Not a duplicate of F101 (store anchored where hoisted @gtkx packages cannot import it) or F306 (`codegen: false` deleting the store through GTKX's own removeShadowingStores) - neither involves an external command pruning the link.

rejected.title: GLib.Regex.match returns a GMatchInfo pointing at the argument string that GTKX has already freed, so every string accessor reads freed heap
rejected.why:
Ruled out by the first criterion: the GLib C API documentation states this behavior, and GTKX faithfully exposes a GLib / GObject-Introspection limitation.

1. The C contract. /usr/share/gir-1.0/GLib-2.0.gir, method g_regex_match, carries GLib's own prose: "`string` is not copied and is used in #GMatchInfo internally. If you use any #GMatchInfo method (except g_match_info_free()) after freeing or modifying `string` then the behaviour is undefined." The same paragraph reaches the user verbatim: /tmp/marshal-replay/node_modules/.gtkx/gi/glib/glib.d.ts lines 11641-11643 (match), 11666-11668 (matchAll), 11715-11717 (matchFull). So the binding documents the retained-subject contract at the exact call the reproduction makes.

2. The GIR annotation GTKX is given is `<parameter name="string" transfer-ownership="none">` on a `utf8`, identical to every other borrowed `const gchar *` in the whole type system. Under the GObject-Introspection annotation contract, transfer-none in-parameters are guaranteed only for the duration of the call; there is no annotation anywhere in GI that expresses "the callee stores this pointer inside an out parameter". GLib's own annotation understates the lifetime its prose demands. GTKX marshals precisely what the annotation declares: packages/native/src/ffi/codec/string.rs, `impl Encoder for StringCodec::encode`, builds a `CString` for the borrowed branch and parks it in `ffi::Stash::Storage`, and packages/native/src/api/call.rs, `execute_call`, drops that `Vec<ffi::Stash>` at return. That is the correct lifetime for a transfer-none in-parameter and is what every other sync call in the codebase depends on.

3. C control, proving this is GLib's documented behavior and not GTKX marshalling. /tmp/regex_ctl.c calls g_regex_match with a g_strdup'd subject and prints fetch(0)/fetch(1) twice, once with the subject alive and once after g_free plus one intervening allocation:
   alive  fetch0=abc123 fetch1=abc
   freed  fetch0=XXXXXX fetch1=XXX
GLib itself hands back the bytes that now occupy the freed block. The garbage in the reproduction is g_match_info_fetch doing exactly what its documentation says it does.

4. Reference-binding cross-check on this same machine and GLib 2.88.1. PyGObject, the reference GObject-Introspection binding, corrupts identically:
   python3 -c "from gi.repository import GLib; r=GLib.Regex.new('([a-z]+)([0-9]+)',0,0); ok,i=r.match('abc123',0); print(i.fetch(0), i.fetch(1), i.fetch(2), i.get_string())"
   -> 'GLib.M' 'GLi' 'b.M' 'GLib.MatchInfo'
Same corruption, different binding, no GTKX code involved. This is a GLib API that automatic introspection cannot bind safely, not a GTKX marshalling defect.

5. Not a duplicate and not a machine artifact. The nearest ledger entry is F203 (round 2, fixed at 5a7c9b57), which is the async case: an argument the callee keeps reading after the call returns, solved by retaining the stashes on the completion callback (AsyncCompletion::retain in packages/native/src/api/call.rs). That mechanism exists only because an async call has a completion callback to hang the retention on and because GI does model async scope. A sync call whose out parameter silently borrows an in parameter offers no such channel. The reproduction was rerun from /tmp/marshal-replay and fails as reported, so the observation is accurate; the judgment is that GTKX marshals correctly and GLib's contract is the source.

The report's own premise, that "a C or gjs caller keeps the subject alive for the lifetime of the GMatchInfo", is exactly the point: that obligation belongs to the caller, GLib declines to copy, and GI provides no way to declare it. The secondary criterion also applies: anything GTKX could do here is a new hand-written GLib.Regex override, a missing feature rather than a broken code path.

rejected.title: The whole GLib.Regex length-taking family types its subject as string[] and marshals it as a char**, so GLib parses the pointer array itself as the text to match
rejected.why:
Ruled out on ground 1 (GTKX faithfully exposes a GLib limitation) and secondarily on ground 5 (missing feature, not a broken path). Not a duplicate of any pre-round-5 ledger entry, and not a machine artifact.

The report reproduces: `node repro/04-regex-string-array.mjs` in a fresh app from the supplied setup.sh printed `Regex.replace ... got " "`, `Regex.splitFull ... got [" "]`, `Regex.matchFull ... got [false,null]`, `Regex.replaceEval ... THROW UTF-8 error: 1 byte missing at end`. So the observation is accurate. The attribution is not.

(1) GTKX transcribes the GLib-supplied annotation exactly. /usr/share/gir-1.0/GLib-2.0.gir (GLib 2.88.1) declares the subject parameter of g_regex_replace at line 35242 as `<array length="1" zero-terminated="0" c:type="const gchar*"><type name="utf8" c:type="gchar"/></array>` — an array whose element type is `utf8`, with the element count in argument 1. `packages/codegen/src/analysis/descriptor-render.ts:704` `arrayExpression` renders a carray with a `lengthParameterIndex` as `tSizedArray(element, ...)`, and `elementExpression` renders a `utf8` element as `t.string("borrowed")`. `t.sizedArray(t.string("borrowed"), 1, "borrowed")` is the literal, correct rendering of what GLib declares. The defect is the missing `(element-type guint8)` on the `(array length=string_len)` annotation in GLib's own glib/gregex.c, which makes g-ir-scanner emit `utf8` for the `gchar` element. That is upstream GLib, not GTKX. Exactly the six occurrences the report counted are present in the GIR (lines 35026, 35137, 35243, 35342, 35416, 35545), all GLib.Regex, all carrying the same upstream annotation error.

(2) The report's central claim for why this is GTKX-specific is empirically false. It asserts "gjs and pygobject both special-case it and expose these parameters as plain strings with the length filled in automatically." pygobject 3.56.3 on this machine, reading the same GIR through libgirepository, does no such thing:

    >>> r = GLib.Regex.new('[0-9]+', 0, 0)
    >>> r.replace('a12b', 0, '#', 0)
    TypeError: Unable to marshal str as an array, use .encode() to convert to bytes
    >>> r.replace(b'a12b', 0, '#', 0)
    TypeError: Must be string, not int
    >>> r.replace(['a12b'], 0, '#', 0)
    gi.repository.GLib.GError: g-regex-error-quark: Error while matching regular expression [0-9]+: UTF-8 error: 2 bytes missing at end
    >>> r.replace_literal(['a12b'], 0, '#', 0)   # and split_full, match_full
    gi.repository.GLib.GError: ... UTF-8 error: 1 byte missing at end

pygobject hides `string_len` exactly as GTKX does, demands a sequence exactly as GTKX does, marshals each element as a utf8 pointer exactly as GTKX does, and produces the same nondeterministic pointer-derived GLib UTF-8 errors. A plain string is rejected there too. The reference GObject-Introspection binding is broken here in precisely the same way, which is direct evidence that this is faithful consumption of a defective upstream annotation rather than a GTKX marshalling error. (gjs is not installed here, but its `gjs_array_to_explicit_array` string special case is restricted to `GI_TYPE_TAG_INT8`/`GI_TYPE_TAG_UINT8` elements and does not cover a `utf8` element either.)

(3) What the report asks for is a capability GTKX has never had: a table of known-bad upstream GIR annotations that codegen overrides. GTKX's one existing acknowledgment of the byte-string idiom, packages/codegen/src/analysis/nul-terminated-bytes.ts, only recognizes `char*` arrays whose element is genuinely `int8`/`uint8` and is consumed solely by `nulTerminatedNote` in packages/codegen/src/store/gi/callable-doc.ts to emit a JSDoc warning. It never touches the emitted descriptor. There is no annotation-correction mechanism to be broken, so this is an absent feature rather than a defective path.

Oracle 6 as applied is also weaker than stated: it is satisfied identically by pygobject, so it separates "GLib annotated this wrong" from nothing at all.

rejected.title: A JS exception thrown from a callback the GLib main loop invokes is neither reported nor cleared, so the loop stops running callbacks and the process hangs forever in silence
rejected.why:
Ruled out on the "reproduction misuses the API in a way the GTKX documentation warns about" ground.

1. Replay notes. A first replay into a fresh /tmp copy printed only "run returned 0" and exited 0, because a stray hung process from the hunter's own ten-run loop (pid 2939846, /home/eugenio/gtkx-playground/replay-marshal-r5-7731) still owns com.gtkx.marshalr5.hang on the session bus, so the replay registered as a remote instance. With a unique ID (com.gtkx.judge.hang1) the hang reproduces exactly as reported: "[app] activate", "[app] throwing callback entered", exit=124, nothing on stderr. So the symptom is not a machine artifact, and it is not a duplicate: no earlier-round entry in .bughunt/findings.jsonl covers a swallowed callback exception (R107 and R108 are the closest, and both were rejected on this same ground).

2. What the code does. packages/native/src/ffi/closure.rs, ClosureData::dispatch (lines 454-467), handles a thrown JS exception by re-throwing it into the environment: `napi::JsError::from(error).throw_into(env.raw())`. That is deliberate propagation, not a dropped error. GTKX collects it at each boundary it owns: packages/native/src/runloop.rs on_prepare wraps every g_main_context_iteration in crate::host::node_env::run_dispatch_scope, and packages/native/src/host/node_env.rs:122 run_dispatch_scope calls report_pending_exception, which does napi_get_and_clear_last_exception + napi_fatal_exception. The other boundary is the return of the JS-to-native call that dispatched the callback, where V8 delivers the pending exception to the JS caller.

Both boundaries work. I verified them directly in /tmp/marshal-replay-judge:
- repro/judge-nodeloop.mjs (same throwing GLib.timeoutAdd callback, Node's loop driving GLib through the uv prepare pump): prints "Error: boom from node-driven loop" with a full stack through runCallback and exits 1.
- repro/judge-iteration.mjs (throwing GLib.timeoutAdd callback, loop stepped with GLib.MainContext.default().iteration(true) from JS): the exception is delivered at that JS call site and is caught by an ordinary try/catch, then the program exits 0.

The only way to lose the exception is to make sure neither boundary is ever reached, which is what g_application_run and g_main_loop_run do: they take the thread away from Node forever, so on_prepare never fires and the call frame that would deliver the exception never returns.

3. Why that is a departure from the documented model. packages/runtime/src/lifecycle.ts:132-134, published as website/reference/@gtkx/runtime/variables/runApplication.md:19-20, states: "g_application_run() is not what starts the application, because it would drive its own main loop and freeze Node; only the local command line handling it delegates to runs here." The repro starts the application with precisely that call. It also constructs a bare Gio.Application rather than createApplication, which runApplication (lifecycle.ts:148-155) refuses by name: "this application was not built by GTKX ... render <GtkApplication> or <AdwApplication>, or construct it with createApplication". website/guide/why-gtkx.md prescribes the same model from the other side: a GTKX app is an ordinary Node.js process, and timers are setTimeout and setInterval. Nothing in the guides, the tutorial, the examples, or the packages themselves ever runs a GLib main loop from JS; the one application.run call in the codebase (application-class.ts:88) is short-circuited by vfuncLocalCommandLine to reach GLib teardown without driving a loop.

4. The reported bar does not hold. The report argues that an unhandled promise rejection in the same GLib source callback proves the runtime can report during a blocking run. It does not. repro/judge-reject.mjs rejects a promise inside a timeoutAdd callback under app.run([]): the output order is "[app] rejecting callback entered", "[app] later callback ran", "run returned 0", and only then the rejection report and exit 1. Node's error reporting is frozen for the whole duration of the blocking run in that case too; it surfaces after run returns. The pending exception behaves the same way, except that it also blocks every later napi call, so the callback that would release the hold cannot run, run never returns, and the deferred report never arrives. That poisoning is the documented "freeze Node" condition compounding itself, not a separate broken path.

5. Every documented way of writing the same program behaves correctly: with Node driving the loop, the identical throwing GLib callback prints a stack and exits 1, and a nested dispatch delivers the exception to a catchable JS call site. The failure needs the one call GTKX's own reference documents that it deliberately never makes.

rejected.title: Removing a JSX prop leaves a registered class's own property at its old value, while inherited props on the same element reset
rejected.why: The report's premise is that reset-on-removal is GTKX's contract and that installed properties are the exception. It is not, and they are not. A control app with no registerClass anywhere (/home/eugenio/gtkx-playground/subclass-r5/repro/judge-label.tsx, built and run under the same headless compositor) shows a plain <GtkLabel> behaving identically: "shipped prop 'label' after removal: \"set\" fresh \"\"", "shipped prop 'cssClasses' after removal: [\"marked\"] fresh []", while widthRequest returns to -1. The framework's own e2e suite pins this as intended at /home/eugenio/gtkx-bughunt/packages/e2e/tests/elements/widget.test.tsx:332 — it("preserves the last-set value when a prop transitions to undefined") rerenders <GtkLabel label={undefined} /> and asserts the old text survives. The cause is structural, in /home/eugenio/gtkx-bughunt/packages/codegen/src/store/jsx/metadata.ts: defaultPropEntry / renderDefaultLiteral emit a defaults row only when the GIR declares a default-value that resolves to a primitive, enum or alias literal, and willSetterRejectNull deliberately withholds the row when writing that default would be rejected by the property's setter; object-, array- and boxed-valued properties get no row at all. GtkLabel:label carries no default-value in /usr/share/gir-1.0/Gtk-4.0.gir:87500 while GtkWidget:width-request does, which is the entire explanation for the A/B the report treats as its oracle. resetPlain in /home/eugenio/gtkx-bughunt/packages/react/src/reconciler/apply-props.ts:55 gating on Object.hasOwn(info.defaults, name) is that policy in code: reset only where a safe declared default is known, otherwise leave the property alone. A registerClass-installed property has no codegen row for the same reason GtkLabel:label has none, so the behavior is uniform rather than an exception. Deriving a reset value from the live GType's installed ParamSpecs at runtime is a mechanism that exists for no property today, so this is a missing feature, not a broken one. website/guide/subclassing.md "Rendering a registered class" says the element inherits the props, defaults and behaviors of every ancestor type, which is exactly what happens (widthRequest resets from GtkWidget's row); it promises nothing about defaults for properties the subclass installs itself, and its only statement about those is that they are applied after construction.

rejected.title: Unmounting an AdwNavigationPage that is on the navigation stack never removes it, so a drill-down leaves a dead page on screen and the next drill-down aborts the app
rejected.why:
Every step of the failure chain is Adwaita's own documented behavior, reproduced with zero React involvement.

I wrote a pure-GI probe (/home/eugenio/gtkx-playground/higapp-r5/repro/navview/pure-gi.test.tsx) that issues by hand exactly the call sequence GTKX's slot issues, using only @gtkx/gi/adw and no reconciler, no JSX elements, no element behaviors:

    view.add(root); view.add(detail1); view.push(detail1);
    view.remove(detail1);   -> visible=Detail stack=[Root, Detail], findPage("detail")=Detail
    view.add(detail2 /* tag "detail" */);
      gtkx: Adwaita-CRITICAL: Duplicate page tag in AdwNavigationView: detail
      detail2.parent after the rejected add = null
    view.remove(detail2);
      gtkx: Adwaita-CRITICAL: adw_navigation_view_remove: assertion 'gtk_widget_get_parent (GTK_WIDGET (page)) == GTK_WIDGET (self)' failed

Both criticals, in the same order and wording the report shows, come out of libadwaita with GTKX's React layer entirely absent. The second half of the probe shows the documented cure: pop() then remove() leaves findPage("detail2")=null and lets the same tag be added again with no critical.

Rule-out 1 (the C API documents this) applies to each link:

- /usr/share/gir-1.0/Adw-1.gir, adw_navigation_view_remove: "Removes @page from @self. If @page is currently in the navigation stack, it will be removed once it's popped. Otherwise, it's removed immediately." The report quotes this itself. GTKX calls remove(); Adwaita defers it. That is the documented contract, not a GTKX omission.
- The children->add() mapping is Adwaita's own: the AdwNavigationView class doc states "`AdwNavigationView` as `GtkBuildable`: AdwNavigationView allows to add pages as children, equivalent to using the [method@NavigationView.add] method." GTKX's JSX-child-to-buildable-child mapping is therefore exact.
- add() is documented as registration only: "Any page that has been added will stay in @self even after being popped... they aren't accessible to the user until [method@NavigationView.push] is called (except for the first page)." So "mounting a second AdwNavigationPage does not navigate to it" is the specified behavior, not a defect.
- The duplicate-tag critical is libadwaita's programmer-error diagnostic, and it makes add() return early before parenting the page, which is why the subsequent remove() then trips the parent assertion. Both are consequences of calling add() with a tag that is still registered because the app never popped.

Rule-out 2 (the reproduction misuses the API): the navigation stack is imperative state the application owns. Adwaita exposes visible-page and visible-page-tag as read-only properties (confirmed in the GIR: no writable="1", getter only), and offers only push/pop/pop_to_page/replace to move the stack. The repro pushes through a ref, so React never learns the page is on the stack, then unmounts it without popping. The report's own workaround.test.tsx fixes it by popping in the child's effect cleanup, which is the correct ownership: whoever pushed must pop.

Rule-out 5 (missing feature, not a broken one): what the report actually wants is a declarative binding of the navigation stack to the React tree (a visiblePageTag prop, or React-driven push/pop). Adwaita provides no settable property to bind to, so that is new GTKX surface, not a repair.

The "GTKX contract" argument does not survive reading the guide it cites. website/guide/modals-and-portals.md:52 and :58 state the mount/unmount contract for windows and for AdwDialog specifically, and GTKX implements exactly those two: packages/react/src/components/window.tsx destroyWindow calls window.destroy(), packages/react/src/adw/dialog.tsx closeDialog calls dialog.forceClose(). No guide states a general "unmounting any element takes its widget off screen" rule, and AdwNavigationPage is neither a window nor a dialog.

Making the detach handler pop would also require GTKX to rewrite navigation state it does not own. A page can sit anywhere in the stack, and the only ways down are pop() (a no-op below two pages), pop_to_page() (which pops and destroys every dynamically pushed page above the target), and replace(). Unmounting a page three levels deep would silently discard the pages above it. That is a modeling mismatch inherent to Adwaita's imperative stack, not a bug in packages/react/src/adw/element-behaviors.ts.

Not a duplicate: no entry in .bughunt/findings.jsonl from rounds 0 through 4 touches AdwNavigationView (F004 and F115 are AdwAlertDialog and AdwDialog). Not a machine artifact: it reproduces from plain Adwaita calls, independent of the compositor, the container, or the codegen store.
